text:
Maya: Heads up — after the route-policy v3 canary went to us-east, we're seeing a spike of traces where downstream client spans are missing. example traceparent I pulled: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
Chris: Same symptom as earlier header-strip issues? roughly what percent and which services?
Maya: ~4% overall, concentrated on api-gateway -> billing-service calls. sps show root + server spans but no client spans.
sre-bot: alert: trace_anomaly rate=3.9% window=5m service=api-gateway tag=missing-client-spans
Olivia: I tried a curl through the canary gateway and saw traceparent at the gateway ingress:
```
> curl -v -H "traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-1234567890abcdef-01" https://canary-gw.us-east/redir
> <- traced at gateway: traceparent=00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-1234567890abcdef-01
```
But the billing pod logs show no trace id and the otel SDK created a new root for the server span.
Jessie: quick grep of the envoy filter we rolled shows a header rewrite rule I didn't expect: it rewrites traceparent -> x-traceparent for downstream routing. snippet: 
```
request_headers_to_add:
  - header: x-traceparent
    value: "%REQ(traceparent)%"
request_headers_to_remove:
  - traceparent
```
That would strip the standard header clients expect.
Daniel: ugh. that explains it. backend SDKs look for traceparent. who approved this change?
Maya: It came from the route-policy team change; canary was intended for multi-tenant header isolation, but we clearly removed forwarding for the standard header.
Chris: Is the exporter affected or just header loss? otel-collector logs show successful exports for spans we saw, but total span counts drop. sample from otelcol: 
```
2026-03-17T21:10:12Z WARN exporter/otlp GRPC error: failed to export spans: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection refused
```
So there were intermittent exporter errors around 21:10 but timeline shows header rewrite deployed at 21:05.
Olivia: I can reproduce locally by applying that envoy snippet — gateway rewrites header and billing SDK starts new trace.
Daniel: Immediate action: pause canary and patch filter to stop removing traceparent. I'll push patch to canary route-policy and remove request_headers_to_remove.
deploy-bot: rollback requested: route-policy v3 canary -> paused (us-east), ticket #INC-4892
Maya: Rolling back now and will run synthetic trace smoke tests after rollback completes.
Jessie: I'll open a PR to change the rewrite to add x-traceparent instead of renaming: leave traceparent, also set x-traceparent for legacy consumers.
Chris: Also add a test in the e2e suite that sends a traceparent and asserts it reaches downstream pod logs.
Olivia: After rollback, I ran a quick test — traces restored for the synthetic flow, client spans reappear. Monitor dashboards for 30m.
Maya: Thanks. Followups: (1) postmortem for why rewrite landed without e2e check, (2) add a linter that flags removal of standard tracing headers, (3) check otelcol exporter errors timeline to confirm no independent outage.
Daniel: I'll pair with infra to correlate deploy times with otelcol errors.
Maya: Ping me if you find anything else. I'll update #incidents if the degraded window grows.
Chris: +1, nice catch. :thumbsup:
Maya: closing thread once dashboards show clean.
